findings.title: An empty continuation response can preserve the same cursor and create a nonterminating pagination command
findings.reproduction: At exact candidate 9910ca3ae717ced397830125381e555901fd5abe, call createCoreApiClient.lineage with the accepted continuation command revisionId=<valid revision>, direction=ancestors, cursor=50, pageSize=50, and maxDepth=8. Have a fake transport return the exact matching revision/direction, integrityState='verified', exportAllowed=true, items=[], and nextCursor=50. The generated client accepts the response. Its request-aware progress guard is `nextCursor !== null && nextCursor !== command.cursor + items.length`; with zero items, the only accepted non-null cursor is therefore the unchanged requested cursor. AuditLineageWorkspace.loadMoreLineage submits trace.nextCursor and mergeLineagePage retains the accepted empty page's nextCursor, so the same Load more action remains enabled and can repeat forever without adding a fact. This contradicts the slice's strict bounded pagination/termination authority and the architecture documentation's claim that non-progress cursors are rejected. The honest Core currently returns null after an empty page, but the generated client is the required cross-process trust boundary and must reject malformed or future-regressed responses.
findings.required_remediation: Require every non-null continuation cursor to make strict forward progress beyond the request cursor and to satisfy an unambiguous contract for the returned page; an empty page must terminate with nextCursor=null. Preserve the existing request-bound item/depth/root/identity guards. Add a fake-transport case for empty same-cursor and backward cursors plus a renderer interaction proving an empty terminal page removes Load more and cannot resubmit the same command.

findings.title: The renderer can export an incomplete trace and can regain export authority while integrity-review remains active
findings.reproduction: At exact candidate 9910ca3ae717ced397830125381e555901fd5abe, pass exportLineageManifest a verified response with exportAllowed=true, exportDenialReason=null, and nextCursor non-null. The function exports immediately; it checks only exportAllowed/denial and serializes the currently loaded items without requiring nextCursor=null or recording that the result is a bounded partial manifest tied to the accepted query. The committed renderer test itself creates an exportable value by shallow-overriding lineage while lineage still has nextCursor=4 and expects export success. Independently, start mergeLineagePage with current.integrityState='integrity-review', exportAllowed=false, and an integrity denial, then merge a valid later page with integrityState='verified', exportAllowed=true, and exportDenialReason=null. The merge preserves the stricter integrity-review state but spreads the later page's export fields, producing integrity-review plus exportAllowed=true/null. exportLineageManifest then exports that inconsistent trace. This violates the approved content-minimized export/redaction workflow and service-level rights/integrity denial: pagination may silently omit governed facts, and integrity-review must remain fail-closed regardless of later page authority.
findings.required_remediation: Make export authority an invariant of the complete accepted trace, not the most recent page. Fail closed whenever integrityState is not verified, any page denies export, page authority is inconsistent, or completeness is not established. Either require the governed export to load and validate every bounded page through termination or explicitly implement a separately authorized partial-export contract that binds the accepted query, cursor range, completeness state, integrity state, and omission notice; the approved current workflow does not authorize silent partial export. Merge export authority monotonically (denial/integrity-review wins) and add actual renderer tests for partial pages, mixed page rights, an integrity-review current trace followed by a verified/allowed page, and successful complete export.
